title: Knowledge Check 2 - Lessons 6-10
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 6-10 - Prompt Engineering. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A requirement is to generate an open-text product recommendation for an agent to use anywhere, drawing on an Account, its Cases, and a custom Asset object, invoked from an Apex action. Which type fits, and why?
options: Field Generation, because it writes to a record
Record Summary, because it summarizes records
Flex, because it defines its own resources, grounds with several objects, and is invoked from Flow, Apex, or a prompt action
Sales Email, because it grounds on a record
questions.explanation: The output is open text used anywhere, the prompt must read several objects, and the entry point is Apex, which together make Flex the only classic type whose binding and entry points fit.

questions.question: A scenario asks for a personalized renewal email to a Contact, with the prompt grounded in the Contact and one related object. Which type is correct?
options: Sales Email, which binds a Contact or a Lead and optionally one more object
Field Generation
Record Summary
Flex, because it is more flexible
questions.explanation: The output is a customer email and the anchor is a Contact, which is exactly the Sales Email binding, so a general type is unnecessary here.

questions.question: A requirement must combine six unrelated objects into one generated result. What is the correct reading?
options: Field Generation, because it writes to a record
Record Summary, because it reads the whole record
Sales Email, with the extra objects as related lists
Flex grounds with up to five objects, so a requirement needing more objects signals the prompt or its architecture needs rethinking
questions.explanation: Flex is the multi-object type and grounds with up to five objects, so exceeding that set points at a design problem rather than a different classic type with a wider binding.

questions.question: An agent must answer policy questions from a library of Knowledge articles, matching on meaning rather than exact keywords. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field that pulls the article title onto the case
A Flow resource that copies the article body onto the record
A Data 360 retriever that indexes the articles and returns the most relevant chunks at run time
An Apex resource that concatenates every article into one field
questions.explanation: A Data 360 retriever indexes unstructured content and performs semantic search over it, returning relevant chunks to the LLM, which is retrieval augmented generation and the right tool for meaning-based matching over a corpus.

questions.question: A reply must always name the customer's account status, a field that already exists on the Contact record. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field that references the record field
A vector retriever over the account documents
An ensemble retriever across all data sources
A prompt flow that recomputes the status from scratch
questions.explanation: A merge field pulls a known field value deterministically and cheaply from the associated record, so a value that already sits on the Contact is a merge field job rather than a retrieval job.

questions.question: Before the agent writes a reply, a discount value must be computed from purchase history on a different object. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field on the Contact record
A Data Library over uploaded files
A vector search index over the history text
A Flow or Apex resource used to ground the prompt with the computed value
questions.explanation: When a value must be computed or fetched across objects before the prompt is built, a Flow or Apex resource grounds the template with that value, whereas merge fields only reach fields on the associated record.

questions.question: A policy page changes daily and an agent must always state the current version. Which grounding approach fits?
options: A vector retriever over the policy documents
An action that reads the current record at run time rather than a retriever over an index
An ensemble retriever across all sources
A merge field on the case that stores a copy of the policy
questions.explanation: A retriever reads an index that refreshes on a schedule, so a fact that changes daily can be served stale, while an action that reads the record at run time always returns the current value.

questions.question: A retriever that returns every article in a huge library produces noisy answers. What is the best fix?
options: Move to a larger model
Rewrite the prompt to say ignore the irrelevant parts
Add a second retriever over the same index
Narrow the retriever to the right source and data space, filter by metadata, chunk by semantic boundary, and return only needed fields
questions.explanation: Over-broad retrieval is a configuration problem, so tightening the source, filters, chunking, and returned fields removes the noise, whereas a larger model or a prompt instruction does not fix a retrieval that returns the wrong passages.

questions.question: A scenario needs a single field value that already exists on the Contact record. Which grounding technique fits?
options: A merge field that references the record field
A vector retriever over contact documents
A Data Library over uploaded files
A prompt flow that recomputes the value each run
questions.explanation: A known field on the associated record is a merge field job, because the value already exists and a merge field pulls it deterministically, while a retriever or a flow adds complexity the scenario does not require.

questions.question: Which two associations does a Field Generation prompt template require when you create it?
options: An object and the specific field to complete
A flow and an Apex class
A data space and a search index
A channel and an agent user
questions.explanation: A Field Generation template helps a user complete a specific field, so it requires both the associated object and the field to complete, while the other template types need only the object.

questions.question: How do you invoke an activated prompt template from a Flow?
options: By pasting the prompt text into a formula resource
By calling it from an Apex trigger only
By adding an Actions element and picking the template from the Prompt Template category
By exporting the template and uploading it to the flow
questions.explanation: Every saved and activated template is exposed as an invocable action, so you add an Actions element and filter by the Prompt Template category, passing the associated record as a related entity where the template needs one.

questions.question: What does the resolved prompt show when you click Save and Preview?
options: The compiled agent graph the runtime executes
The template with its merge fields replaced by the selected record's real data, which is what is sent to the LLM
The list of versions saved for the template
The permission sets that can see the template
questions.explanation: The resolved prompt is the template after prompt resolution replaces the placeholders with real org data, and it represents exactly what reaches the LLM, which is why testing it against a sample record matters.

questions.question: A consultant activates version 1 of a template, then needs to change its wording. What must they do?
options: Edit version 1 directly, because it is the active version
Save as a New Version and edit that, because version 1 is now immutable
Deactivate the template, edit version 1, then reactivate it
Delete version 1 and create a new template
questions.explanation: Activation makes a version immutable and even a deactivated but formerly active version stays immutable, so the only way to change the prompt is to save a new version and edit that.

questions.question: What does activating a prompt template version actually do?
options: It makes that version the one available to consuming surfaces, and only one version can be active at a time
It sends the prompt to the model once to warm it up
It copies the template into every agent that references it
It converts the template into an Apex class
questions.explanation: Activation selects which single version is available to the surfaces that call the template, so it is a control over availability and not a change to the template content.

questions.question: An agent is running an active template and someone edits the prompt. What do users see?
options: The edited prompt on the next turn, because editing is immediate
An error until the template is reactivated
A blend of the old and new prompt
The currently active version unchanged, until a new version is activated
questions.explanation: Running surfaces resolve against the active version, so a draft edit is invisible to them and the switch happens only when a different version is activated.
